topics.topic: Segment reporting and margin disclosure methodology
topics.stated_position: "We do not have business operating segments. We have one reportable segment, but disclose revenue by type and product area, to provide useful information to shareholders." Relative margin discussion is "directional and based on estimates" because of central cost pools whose allocation "may also change over time."
topics.quote: We do not have business operating segments. We have one reportable segment, but disclose revenue by type and product area, to provide useful information to shareholders.

topics.topic: Risks to restoring adjusted operating margin above 20%
topics.stated_position: "We remain focused on improving our adjusted operating margin over time to be more consistent with historical peaks," but "the biggest risks continue to be market-related." Long-term value creation is expected from Morningstar Wealth, Workplace, Morningstar Indexes, and DBRS Morningstar, "even if they are subject to cyclical pressure."
topics.quote: Despite these short-term pressures, we believe our strategies in product areas like Morningstar Wealth, Workplace, Morningstar Indexes, and DBRS Morningstar will drive long-term value creation, even if they are subject to cyclical pressure.

topics.topic: Cyclicality of DBRS Morningstar and willingness to spend
topics.stated_position: "We acknowledge that the credit ratings business is a cyclical one," and given weakness "we're managing expenses prudently. That said, we want to be ready when markets rebound and have made investments to support middle-market and private corporate ratings in the U.S. and Europe." Also notes DBRS Morningstar "has a lower proportion of recurring revenue than its larger competitors."
topics.quote: We acknowledge that the credit ratings business is a cyclical one. Given continued weakness in global ratings activity, and, in particular, in structured finance, we’re managing expenses prudently. That said, we want to be ready when markets rebound and have made investments to support middle-market and private corporate ratings in the U.S. and Europe.

topics.topic: DBRS Morningstar competitive position and market share
topics.stated_position: Market-leading positions in Canada; "solid market share in the structured finance sectors in which it is active"; share in CMBS ranged 40-50% per the SEC NRSRO report, but "we've seen some market share pressure in CMBS following the highs noted in the report." Outside Canada, corporate/FI share "is much smaller as we are not a significant player in rating the large, investment-grade corporates," with focus instead on middle-market and private transactions.
topics.quote: DBRS Morningstar’s share of ratings in corporate and financial institutions markets outside of Canada is much smaller as we are not a significant player in rating the large, investment-grade corporates in the U.S. and Europe that dominate the markets. Instead, our focus is on middle-market and private transactions.

topics.topic: DBRS headcount investment and path back to company-average margins
topics.stated_position: "we have invested behind the business over the past several years given the significant market opportunity we see to grow and capture share in a $7.7 billion credit ratings market"; headcount grew to "a little over 800 employees as of the end of 2022," roughly half of the growth in India. "We expect these investments to deliver strong long-term returns and deliver margin improvement over time."
topics.quote: To support these objectives, DBRS Morningstar headcount had grown to a little over 800 employees as of the end of 2022, primarily reflecting additional operational and analytical roles.

topics.topic: PitchBook client vulnerability in a downturn
topics.stated_position: "the client segment that is most vulnerable in the current environment is the company segment, and, in particular start-ups and corporate development teams," which is "about a third of PitchBook's client count"; focus is on educating corporate development teams on additional use cases.
topics.quote: That said, the client segment that is most vulnerable in the current environment is the company segment, and, in particular start-ups and corporate development teams. In total, the company segment represents about a third of PitchBook’s client count, which doesn’t necessarily correspond to its share of revenue.

topics.stated_position: Primary competitors are CB Insights, Preqin, and S&P Capital IQ; "We believe that we can meet the needs of these competitors' core customers all within the PitchBook platform, giving us room to grow to a larger size than any one of these companies/segments alone." With LCD, also competing with LevFin Insights, Refinitiv, and Debtwire.
topics.quote: We believe that we can meet the needs of these competitors’ core customers all within the PitchBook platform, giving us room to grow to a larger size than any one of these companies/segments alone.

topics.stated_position: Two options — seat-based and enterprise licenses. "Over time, we have increased the number of firms on enterprise licenses and expect significant revenue growth to come from continuing to pursue this strategy." Prices were raised in mid-2022.
topics.quote: Over time, we have increased the number of firms on enterprise licenses and expect significant revenue growth to come from continuing to pursue this strategy. Pricing is all-inclusive for the platform and reflects the value we offer to clients.

topics.stated_position: "We have highest penetration among investment banks and the greatest opportunity with the large universe of non-investment bank service providers." TAM built from number of qualifying firms and an estimate of average account revenue across all user types; "we don't see significant differences in product usage statistics by user type."
topics.quote: We have highest penetration among investment banks and the greatest opportunity with the large universe of non-investment bank service providers. We build our estimate of the TAM based on the number of firms that meet our criteria and an estimate of average account revenue across all user types.

topics.topic: LCD acquisition price multiple and expected return
topics.stated_position: "We do not disclose expected ROI on individual transactions, but following extensive due diligence, we expect the acquisition of Leveraged Commentary & Data (LCD) to generate strong returns well above our cost of capital. So far, despite volatility in the credit markets, we are tracking slightly ahead of plan."
topics.quote: We do not disclose expected ROI on individual transactions, but following extensive due diligence, we expect the acquisition of Leveraged Commentary & Data (LCD) to generate strong returns well above our cost of capital. So far, despite volatility in the credit markets, we are tracking slightly ahead of plan, which reflects the importance of LCD data to clients.

topics.stated_position: Integration of LCD into PitchBook "provides the opportunity to better penetrate PitchBook's existing addressable market as we are able to support expanded client use cases." TAM estimated at $4.9 billion as of April 2022 growing to $6.5 billion as of April 2023. For Morningstar Indexes, opportunity to launch new investable products based on LCD data.
topics.quote: As of April 2022, we estimated that PitchBook’s total TAM was $4.9 billion; as of April 2023, we estimated the TAM grew to $6.5 billion.

topics.topic: Sustainalytics independent investigation into anti-Israel bias concerns
topics.stated_position: "The investigation found no evidence of pervasive or systemic bias across Sustainalytics' products, but offered helpful process and procedure recommendations that Morningstar is implementing to reinforce transparency, consistency, and objectivity in our work." Investigation conducted by White & Case; legal fees "were a meaningful part of our increase in professional fees in 2022."
topics.quote: The investigation found no evidence of pervasive or systemic bias across Sustainalytics’ products, but offered helpful process and procedure recommendations that Morningstar is implementing to reinforce transparency, consistency, and objectivity in our work.

topics.topic: Accountability for returns on recent large acquisitions
topics.stated_position: "We have largely financed these acquisitions with additional debt, which has contributed to short-term negative impacts on our return on invested capital (ROIC) as invested capital has increased with returns expected to improve in future periods." DBRS Morningstar "was tracking ahead of plan through 2021" before market headwinds; Sustainalytics revenue "has exceeded plan, although we have invested more heavily than initially anticipated."
topics.quote: We have largely financed these acquisitions with additional debt, which has contributed to short-term negative impacts on our return on invested capital (ROIC) as invested capital has increased with returns expected to improve in future periods.

topics.topic: Evolution of M&A approach under current management
topics.stated_position: "Our approach to acquisitions has remained consistent over time. We favor organic growth but remain opportunistic when we identify transactions that can complement our strategy and provide strong returns." 40 acquisitions in 15 years, 12 since 2017; "the size of the transactions has increased in recent years" and "As our business and balance sheet grow, we can pursue larger transactions if they meet our criteria."
topics.quote: Our approach to acquisitions has remained consistent over time. We favor organic growth but remain opportunistic when we identify transactions that can complement our strategy and provide strong returns. In the past 15 years, we have completed 40 acquisitions, with 12 having closed since 2017.

topics.topic: Exposure to SVB Financial, Signature Bank and First Republic Bank
topics.stated_position: "PitchBook did have a relationship with SVB Financial and Signature Bank, as well as with First Republic Bank... While all three relationships were important, we do not consider the revenue from these clients to be material to PitchBook's overall revenue base." PitchBook is the only product with direct exposure to PE/VC markets.
topics.quote: While all three relationships were important, we do not consider the revenue from these clients to be material to PitchBook’s overall revenue base.

topics.topic: Artificial intelligence as friend or foe
topics.stated_position: "We view advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a "friend" to Morningstar's business. Our data collections operations are already heavily automated and integrate GPT technology." Rolling out an AI chatbot powered by editorial content and fund and equity reports, targeted at advisors and asset managers.
topics.quote: We view advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a “friend” to Morningstar’s business. Our data collections operations are already heavily automated and integrate GPT technology.

topics.topic: Net zero commitment and science-based targets
topics.stated_position: As an NZFSPA signatory, "Morningstar is committed to taking steps to achieve net zero by 2050." "Morningstar's current targets are considered 'science-based' because they are in line with what the latest climate science deems necessary to meet the goals of the Paris Agreement." Near-term goals include a first TCFD-aligned report; longer-term, SBTi certification.
topics.quote: Our near-term goals include publication of our first TCFD-aligned report, which we are prioritizing as part of our commitment to the NZFSPA. Over the longer-term, our goals include certification of our efforts by the SBTi.

notable_language.quote: We would note that as of 2022, DBRS Morningstar has a lower proportion of recurring revenue than its larger competitors.
notable_language.why_notable: An unusually direct concession about a structural disadvantage versus larger ratings competitors.

notable_language.quote: We’d note that in addition to a large issuance declines, we’ve seen some market share pressure in CMBS following the highs noted in the report as the mix of transaction types in this space has changed, along with our prevailing credit views.
notable_language.why_notable: Admission of share erosion in the asset class where DBRS's position was strongest, hedged with an attribution to 'prevailing credit views.'

notable_language.quote: As we assess our progress in reaching our objectives with DBRS Morningstar, the biggest challenge has been the sharp slowdown in ratings activity starting in mid-2022, although we believe that we are well-positioned to grow when credit issuance picks up.
notable_language.why_notable: Characterises the DBRS shortfall as external and cyclical rather than strategic — a framing that recurs throughout the filing.

notable_language.quote: Overall, revenue has exceeded plan, although we have invested more heavily than initially anticipated to capitalize on long-term opportunities that materialized post-acquisition.
notable_language.why_notable: Rare acknowledgement on Sustainalytics that spending outran the original acquisition case, framed as opportunity rather than overrun.

notable_language.quote: While larger transactions can create more meaningful value, smaller transactions can be equally as important to our strategy and can often take as much time to integrate as some of the larger deals we’ve done.
notable_language.why_notable: Defends a shift toward larger deals while insisting the underlying approach is unchanged — a hedge on the acquisitiveness question.

notable_language.quote: These methodologies are not complete and, like our product areas, do change from time to time. As a result, our discussions of relative margins are directional and based on estimates.
notable_language.why_notable: A standing caveat that limits the reliability of any product-level profitability figure management gives; repeated later in the document.
